subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration (SDK + function calling + streaming)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Daniel Lee <daniel.lee@acmecorp.com>
Date: Sat, 31 Jul 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration (SDK + function calling + streaming)

Hi Sofia / Daniel —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of what we covered and agreed next steps so we’re aligned:

Pain points you called out
- High per-token costs on current provider for multi-turn support and embeddings-heavy reranks
- Latency spikes at peak QPS (search + assistant flows) causing client-side timeouts
- Need for structured outputs from assistant responses to drive downstream workflows (JSON payloads)

Goals
- Reduce unit inference cost by ~30% while keeping quality on par
- Sub-300ms p90 for assistant path at 5 RPS target per instance type
- Reliable embeddings + reranking flow for semantic search across 200M docs

Integration notes / product fit
- SDK: minimal changes expected — our JS/Go SDKs support streaming and structured output hooks. We recommend integrating with our streaming SDK to reduce perceived latency for users who render incremental tokens.
- Function calling: can map directly to your existing action handlers. We discussed using function-calling to trigger the structured JSON payloads you need for order/extract flows.
- Structured outputs: Redwood supports constrained generation + schema enforcement (JSON Schema) to ensure machine-parseable outputs.
- Embeddings / reranking: we can run embeddings on a cheaper quantized variant and run a lightweight reranker on a higher-quality variant for top-K scoring (we discussed 2-stage).
- Streaming + KV cache: enabling prefix caching for repeated prompts should reduce token spend on frequent queries.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short integration proposal and a suggested network architecture diagram for Private deployment (redwood-integration-proposal.pdf, network-architecture.png).

Action items (owners & ETA)
1) Marissa: send detailed cost/latency estimate and proposed plan for PoC (by Mon 8/2) — DONE (attached proposal)
2) Acme: confirm dataset size for embeddings indexing and initial rerank sample (Sofia) — by Tue 8/3
3) Technical sync: 60-min PoC kickoff with Redwood infra + Acme infra (target Thu 8/5) — tentative, please confirm

Question for you now — for the PoC, do you want us to run embeddings and reranking in your VPC (Private) or on Redwood hosted with a strict data retention policy? Both options valid; we can share pros/cons in the kickoff.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

- Dataset size: we’re looking at ~200M short documents (~40M unique paragraphs). We also have daily delta updates (~10k/day).
- For security/compliance, we prefer Private deployment in our AWS VPC for the initial PoC. We’ll need to run a quick checklist (SOC2 + network peering details).
- Rerank flow: we want the two-stage approach you outlined. Daniel will share a sample of ~5k queries + gold rankings for initial eval.

Confirming the PoC kickoff time on Thu 8/5 — can we do 11:00 AM PT? Also, please send the cost/latency estimate and any prerequisites we should prepare.

On the function-calling/structured outputs: we’ll want strict JSON schema validation so our downstream systems don’t need additional parsing. Good to hear you support that.
